summary: Explains `--start-at-task` to begin a playbook at a named task, usually the one that failed last time. Implicit play-level fact gathering and argument validation still run first, and it doesn't work with tasks inside `include_*` roles or tasks.
questions: How do I restart a playbook from the task that failed?
Why can't --start-at-task find my task inside an included role?

answer_card.title: Start at a specific task
answer_card.answer_md:
```shell
ansible-playbook playbook.yml --start-at-task="install packages"
```
Execution starts at the task named "install packages". If that play has play-level fact gathering or argument validation, those implicit tasks still run first.

It does **not** work with tasks inside dynamically reused roles or tasks (`include_*`); use step mode to skip tasks or the playbook debugger to redo them.
